repairs_this_round.R1: The only change in this round is a test-counting defect, and no production code was touched at all. TargetRootReplacedByAFileAfterTheFirstHashIsRefused used a single `hashed` counter for two different meanings and asserted Assert.AreEqual(1, hashed), but the wrapper invokes its callback after EVERY real hash, so a real run that reads four files reached 4 and the assertion failed early -- even though the root had been swapped at the right moment and the run had correctly been refused. The test now keeps three counters apart: `hashCalls` increments after every real hash and is NEVER asserted to a fixed number (the package's file count is not this scenario's property, so 4 is not hardcoded); `flipCount` increments only after the swap really happened; `flipAfterHashCall` records which hash call the swap followed. Only the hashCalls == 1 callback performs the swap, inside this test's own sandbox after proving the absolute path lies under the fixture root; later hashes still go through the real hasher but do not swap again. The closing assertions are flipCount == 1, flipAfterHashCall == 1, hashCalls >= flipAfterHashCall and hashCalls > 0, which proves the root was replaced exactly once and only after a real read had returned, without binding the expectation to the fixture's file count. Every existing assertion is kept verbatim: the root really is a regular file, the run is Rejected with unsafe_path, target_exists is NOT reported, VerifiedFileCount is 0, every location stays relative with no absolute path, and the destructive step self-proves it stays inside this test's sandbox. Nothing was deleted, skipped or weakened, MediaPackageSandbox was not modified, and no public observation interface was added. The wrapper's comment now states accurately that the callback runs once per real hash and that deciding which call swaps is the test's job.
repairs_this_round.R2: The six tracking documents are calibrated against the fifth validation, without rewriting the whole history: the six-failure classification of the third round is now taken directly from docs/development/reviews/TS-099-r3-review-2026-09-21.md instead of being re-summarised (that report records the target root replaced by a regular file as a REAL product defect, the rest as test-construction problems, and the one-byte read-budget change as an adjacent construction correction); acd8eb6a is recorded as the FOURTH candidate and 68a278c as the FIFTH, instead of being conflated; the two different counts are separated explicitly -- 128 test METHODS (70 of them this card's) versus 134 EXPANDED results in the coordinator's real run -- and the coordinator's 134/131/1/2 numbers are marked as coordinator-environment measurements that DSH never executed; unexecuted formal regressions are kept apart from the out-of-tree probe that really ran; and the duplicate-path description was corrected to match what the test actually asserts (it re-parses the mutated bytes and asserts both paths are present and that the path count equals the mutated array length, NOT the stronger 'exactly one more than the original' claim that was never asserted). The remaining long-file observation stays a quality note with no invented exemption. delivery.json keeps a single string source_snapshot pointer, working_tree_clean stays false, head_commit_contains_the_repairs stays false, and both coordinator commit flags stay true.

technical_debt: MediaPackageIssueSink now refuses a new pair past the cap BEFORE storing anything, so both the dedup store and the code list are bounded by MaximumIssues; the regression that pins this counts the private collections through reflection, which is test-side coupling to a private field name and would need updating if the sink's internals are renamed.

IsolatedMediaPackageInspector retains each observed file's length and last-write stamp in a private record and re-observes the target and its trusted parent at the end of the run, so a same-size rewrite and a target root replaced by a file are both refused rather than reported as inspected.

MediaPackageManifestReader decides string well-formedness by making the JSON reader decode every property name and string value; a decode failure becomes invalid_manifest@surrogate_escape and the framework exception is discarded.
MaximumEnumeratedEntries (4096) remains a constant rather than a configurable limit, so an oversized staging directory fails with budget_exceeded instead of a tuned path.
Several CA1506 suppressions carry written justifications; they can be reclaimed once a composition root exists.
